title: Hamilton Beats Washington at the Horn
dek: Washington's first lead came with 33.2 seconds left. After two UConn misses in the final seconds, Richard Hamilton got the ball back and hit a fadeaway at the buzzer.

setup.text: UConn had won the Big East's regular-season and tournament titles and 10 straight games. At 31-4 the Huskies were ranked sixth and seeded second in the East, led by Richard Hamilton, the Big East Player of the Year as a sophomore, and Khalid El-Amin, a freshman point guard.

Washington was the region's surprise. The 11th seed, fourth in the Pac-10, had beaten sixth-seeded Xavier and 14th-seeded Richmond to reach the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1984, and it brought a five-game winning streak to Greensboro.

The two Huskies had never met. UConn had reached a regional final in 1990 and 1995 and lost both times, and it had never been to a Final Four; North Carolina had already beaten Michigan State in the evening's first semifinal.

story.text: UConn led 47-39 at halftime and 64-55 with 10:16 left after a three-point play by Souleymane Wane.
Washington answered with eight straight points while UConn missed five shots and turned it over three times, and it was 64-63 with 7:28 to play.

Hamilton's 3-pointer with 5:54 left and two Jake Voskuhl free throws pushed the lead back to six, but UConn would not make another field goal until the final minute. A 5-0 Washington run made it 69-68 with 2:51 left.

Hamilton scored 18 of his 22 points in the second half, and El-Amin had 19 on 7-of-20 shooting. For Washington, Donald Watts played all 40 minutes and scored 22, Todd MacCulloch had 18 and Deon Luton 17.

sequence.text: A 5-0 Washington run cuts UConn's lead to one.
Hamilton's two free throws make it 71-68, then Watts sets up Patrick Femerling for a layup.
Todd MacCulloch makes one of two free throws, and the game is tied.
Hamilton's rebound basket, UConn's first field goal since 5:54, puts the Huskies back in front.
Donald Watts hits a 3-pointer from the left wing. Washington leads for the first time all night.
El-Amin dribbles near midcourt until about 10 seconds remain, then drives and passes to Jake Voskuhl, whose short shot rims out.

Hamilton rebounds and shoots, but it rolls in and out. The ball is tipped back (by Kevin Freeman, the New York Times reported) and Hamilton has it again. El-Amin sees 1.8 on the clock and tells him to shoot.
Hamilton fades away over 7-foot Patrick Femerling, and the shot drops just as the horn goes off. It is the first buzzer-beater of his life, and his teammates bury him in a pile on the floor.

quotes.text: I gathered myself, let the ball go and it went in.
I knew it was going in as soon as he shot it.
In a season of buzzer-beaters, we add our name to the list.
People won't remember the record, but they'll remember this team and this game.

aftermath.text: Washington's season ended at 20-10. Coach Bob Bender said he told his players they had put themselves in Husky history.
Two nights later, in the same building, top-seeded and top-ranked North Carolina beat UConn 75-64 in the East Regional final, ending the Huskies' season at 32-5.
Hamilton and El-Amin were named to the East Regional all-tournament team.

legacy.text: As the AP noted that night, it was the second time in the decade that a buzzer-beater had sent UConn to a regional final, eight years after Tate George's shot against Clemson.

A year later UConn won its first national championship, and Hamilton was the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player. UConn's own media guide later described the 1997-98 team as having set the stage for that title run.
